technology.summary:
Today's technology news includes a review of the Telo MT1, America's smallest electric truck, which has a cab-over design and is said to turn heads. LG has released a 75-inch RGB LED TV, but the article suggests that OLEDs are still better. Other articles include a review of an AI bird feeder, a list of AI agents that can live in text messages, and a report on AI agent makers promising privacy.

finance.summary:
The Securities and Exchange Board of India and the Reserve Bank of India have teamed up to make it easier for foreign portfolio investors to enter the market. The launch of the India Market Access portal in September 2025 marked a significant step forward in this initiative.

However, global uncertainty has impacted the market and investor sentiment remains cautious. Benchmark indices faced a decline, with the Nifty index under pressure. Indian equity benchmarks experienced a decline over two sessions due to profit booking and rising oil prices.

In other news, a resurgent El Niño pattern risks deepening a selloff in Southeast Asian bonds, threatening to push yields higher just as rising US Treasury rates and oil prices squeeze regional debt.

Finally, hospital stocks slipped after the Supreme Court of India highlighted troubling markups on cancer drugs enforced by hospitals, urging a probe into reports of patients being directed to specific pharmacies for their medications.

politics.summary:
The Delhi High Court has dismissed pleas for a SIT probe into the 2020 riots and 2019 Jamia violence. The Supreme Court will list a plea to allow peaceful protests at Jantar Mantar, where protesters are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Congress claims that tribal students headed for a Mumbai protest were detained and threatened with police cases.

Meanwhile, Donald Trump has cited a non-existent Indian election to call the US electoral process 'corrupt'. Jairam Ramesh has attacked the CEC for executing illegal orders, while Koel Mallick has joined the BJP. India's foreign exchange reserves have reportedly declined by USD 18.34 billion in a single week.
